# Descartes — Meditations on First Philosophy (CSM II, 1984)

## Bibliographic identity

The selected English carrier is *The Philosophical Writings of Descartes*, volume II, translated by John Cottingham, Robert Stoothoff and Dugald Murdoch (Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1984) — **CSM II** — containing the *Meditations on First Philosophy* (Latin original: *Meditationes de prima philosophia*, Paris, 1641). All locators in this house are given as **AT pagination** (Charles Adam and Paul Tannery, eds., *Œuvres de Descartes*, vol. VII) alongside CSM II pages, per the source-bank standard for Descartes. The house was created for the conjugate-field second pass (2026-09-07) per the landing proposal. Bibliographic identity is catalogue-verified; **no copy has been consulted and no wording extracted. Locators are recorded; quotations are not pre-fabricated.**

## Chicago 18 forms

**Full note:** René Descartes, *Meditations on First Philosophy*, in *The Philosophical Writings of Descartes*, vol. 2, trans. John Cottingham, Robert Stoothoff, and Dugald Murdoch (Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1984), {AT VII page / CSM II page}.

**Shortened note:** Descartes, *Meditations*, {AT / CSM II page}.

**Bibliography:** Descartes, René. *Meditations on First Philosophy*. In *The Philosophical Writings of Descartes*, vol. 2. Translated by John Cottingham, Robert Stoothoff, and Dugald Murdoch. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1984.

## Source scholarship

The *Meditations* establish the doubting context (Meditation I: the senses deceived, the dream argument, the deceiving deceiver), reach the indubitable occurrence at the threshold of Meditation II (in thinking, doubting or being deceived, there is presence; the "let him deceive me as much as he can" movement), and then perform the move this house exists to index: from the occurrence to the thinking-thing — *res cogitans* — "a thing that doubts, understands, affirms, denies, is willing, is unwilling, and also imagines and has sensory perceptions." The essay's reading, already argued on its own ground, receives this double movement exactly: the finding is heard correctly; the inference gathers the I into the act too quickly, and the essay's crossed zero names what that gathering did — the slash treated as the I, the zero behind it covered over, `Ø` at position #1 of the recognition-matheme (Taylor, core theorems §IX; see the [core-theorems house](../../../internal-corpus/taylor/taylor-2026-core-theorems-pithy/taylor-2026-core-theorems-pithy.md) for the fuller accounting). **Hume sits at the same position** (finding only the impressions the slash produced and calling the zero empty); Descartes and Hume differ over which side of `Ø` they fixate on.

This summary is orientation, not quotation; the wording of every named site is fixed only at extraction from the edition in hand.

## Essay use

### Source's relevant contribution

The canonical historical site of the operation the essay derives natively: the indubitable heard correctly and the thinking-thing inferred from it. The landing is *beside* Ø-occlusion — the essay's home-grown conceptual form already carries the operation, and Descartes lands alongside it, providing the historical site the essay's form reads. This house gives that landing its citation spine and passage ledger so the A/C root's grounding and any C01/A34/A01 sharpenings can point at recoverable text instead of floating attribution.

### Licensed essay use

- Establish the doubting context (Meditation I) for the dream/illusion/simulation lineage and the computational veil.
- Index the indubitable occurrence: the finding the essay receives correctly (fact of presence; contents remain determinate).
- Index the **reification site**: the move from occurrence to *res cogitans* — the passage `Ø` reads.
- Support the historical register of the Zero/Subject history (modernity at chronic #1-fixation) as a *rereading of the sequence*, never as a claim about Descartes' intention.

### Claim boundary

Descartes is the canonical site of the fusion, **not** the source of the correction. The essay's fact/contents discrimination, its un-reifying reading of the cogito, and the crossed-zero notation are the essay's own argued operations; they are no more attributed to Descartes than QL is attributed to Lacan. No historical thesis about Descartes' intention is asserted anywhere the essay consumes this house. Source relations: *Extracted* once passages are verified against the edition; *Argued from* for the un-reifying reading.

## Passage card — `descartes-1641-meditations-q002` — the reification site
^descartes-1641-meditations-q002

> *(Lead — no quotation until extraction.)* "But what then am I?" — the move from the occurrence to *res cogitans*: a thing that doubts, understands, affirms, denies, wills, refuses, imagines, senses.

- **Locator:** **AT VII 27–28 / CSM II 18–19** — the passage `Ø` reads.
- **Status:** locator recorded; unextracted.
- **Verification:** none this cycle; extraction against CSM II required.
- **Source relation:** toward Extracted.
- **Evidential action:** supports (as the site of the operation the essay names, not as endorsement of the essay's naming).
- **Argument function:** the canonical site of the fusion — the slash gathered into the I; the thinking-thing a content names mistaken for the presence contents appear in.
- **Consumers:** proposed — A/C root A face; A34 sharpening per the landing proposal; Zero/Subject history.
- **Use boundary:** the Ø-reading is the essay's; this passage supplies the historical text it reads, and no intention-claim about Descartes travels with it.

- **Status:** locator recorded; unextracted.
- **Verification:** none this cycle; extraction against CSM II required.
- **Source relation:** toward Extracted.
- **Evidential action:** supports.
- **Argument function:** joins the dream/illusion/simulation lineage — dream proving that objectivity cannot mean externally material; the computational veil; [[Dreamcode]] naming debt.
- **Consumers:** proposed — the A14 dream-reading family; A/C root A face, grounding 5.
- **Use boundary:** supplies the historical doubting context; the essay's dream-simulation lineage is its own development.
